text: make a script to clean them up, present it in the ui like the notification for rebuilding when there are orphans
resolution: Built orphan dev-host detection and cleanup, surfaced in the editor as a notice matching the existing rebuild one. The problem it names is invisibility: a rjit dev run that dies without taking its host down leaves it running and reparented to init, holding no window and serving no socket, so nine had accumulated since Aug 2 holding 4.7GB while the user correctly believed they had one app. rjit orphans reports, --kill retires, --json feeds the notice. A pid is called an orphan only when three independent facts agree — reparented to init, not the dev socket listener, and holding no dmabuf or display-server handle — and any host failing one is kept with the reason printed. Safety drove every decision: there is no pattern form at all, because pkill -f over this repo path matches the polling shell running it and cascades, which is the 2026-04-22 incident that killed all 14 panes; the scan matches the executable rather than a command line mentioning it, with a test proving a pkill shell is not self-matched, and kills are exact numeric pids signalled one at a time with each re-verified immediately beforehand. One measured correction landed mid-build: the first window test counted /dev/dri/renderD128 and spared all nine orphans, because every GPU-initialised process holds it — the honest signal is a dmabuf, which the live host had three of and the orphans none, and that is now a test. The UI never signals a process: it shows the exact pids, says this app is not among them, and writes a one-shot token bound to that pid set which the dev supervisor acts on. 13 tests pass and the live scan correctly kept the user's app and found the nine orphans; nothing was killed, since that is the user's click.
